question: A patient with severe swallowing difficulties and chronic heartburn is scheduled for an upper GI diagnostic test. Which condition would make you question an order for a standard barium swallow?

options.A: A suspected tear in the wall of the esophagus
options.B: A past history of childhood asthma
options.C: A reported fear of small enclosed spaces
options.D: Mild discomfort after eating heavy meals

explanation: A suspected tear means perforation is possible, which completely rules out barium due to the risk of severe tissue damage from leaked contrast. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the main use of short-acting beta-agonists (SABAs) in asthma care?

options.A: Preventing mucus production over a twenty-four hour period
options.B: Providing quick relief during sudden acute bronchospasm
options.C: Curing the underlying chronic inflammation in the lungs
options.D: Rebuilding damaged lung tissue caused by frequent infections

explanation: SABAs act fast during sudden breathlessness, which is why patients carry them around as their reliable rescue inhalers. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important to watch the client's face during passive exercises?

options.A: To check if they are watching the television
options.B: To spot hidden pain or distress when they cannot speak well
options.C: To check how fast their hair is growing
options.D: To see if they need spectacles to read

explanation: Wonderful! Many patients can't tell you when it hurts, so a quick wince or frown on their face tells you everything you need to know. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h6)

question: What does intersectoral collaboration mean in community health practice?

options.A: Transferring all sick patients directly to tertiary teaching hospitals without delay
options.B: Working together with non-health sectors like agriculture and education to improve health
options.C: Merging all community health clinics under one central government ministry
options.D: Requiring nurses to perform the duties of doctors and pharmacists simultaneously

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration involves partnering with different sectors outside health because social determinants of health span multiple fields. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h7)

question: What are the two primary organs that make up the central nervous system?

options.A: Nerves and ganglia
options.B: Spinal cord and peripheral nerves
options.C: Brain and spinal cord
options.D: Cerebrum and cerebellum

explanation: The central nervous system is strictly composed of the brain and the spinal cord, separating it from the peripheral nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h1)

question: What does it usually mean if a patient's deep tendon reflex is very weak or missing entirely?

options.A: Hyperactive function of the spinal cord
options.B: Severe brain injury in the cerebral cortex
options.C: Excessive physical activity of the limb
options.D: Lower motor neuron or peripheral nerve damage

explanation: When a reflex pathway in the limbs is damaged or blocked, the physical response becomes sluggish or disappears. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h8)

question: What is the main study of pharmacology?

options.A: The legal distribution of controlled substances in hospitals
options.B: How chemical substances interact with living systems
options.C: Surgical techniques used alongside medicinal treatments
options.D: The commercial manufacturing and packaging of herbal remedies

explanation: You've got this! Pharmacology simply looks at how drugs and chemicals affect living bodies. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T2#GNS125_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which complication can happen immediately right after FGM is performed?

options.A: Trapped menstrual blood over many years
options.B: Obstetric fistula during childbirth
options.C: Severe hemorrhage and shock
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain in adulthood

explanation: Spot on! Heavy bleeding and sudden shock are dangerous, life-threatening emergencies that can happen right when the cutting takes place. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is another common name for prenatal care?

options.A: Neonatal monitoring
options.B: Postpartum care
options.C: Gynecological screening
options.D: Antenatal care

explanation: Prenatal care is widely referred to as antenatal care, representing health services provided during the period of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h1)

question: Which ethical principle simply means the duty to do no harm to your patient?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Non-maleficence
options.C: Justice
options.D: Beneficence

explanation: Non-maleficence is just a big word for a simple rule: do no harm. As a nurse, you always make sure your actions or mistakes don't cause unnecessary pain or suffering. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h2)

question: Where does a QA committee usually gather its data to check hospital performance?

options.A: Personal diary entries written by hospital visitors
options.B: Weather forecasts and local market price lists
options.C: Social media gossip and daily newspaper headlines
options.D: Patient feedback forms, pharmacy logs, and health records

explanation: Correct! Reliable data comes straight from official hospital records and direct feedback from our patients. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which side effect is commonly linked to the long-term use of Tenofovir?

options.A: Sudden visual blindness
options.B: Kidney and bone toxicity
options.C: Severe permanent hair loss
options.D: Chronic high blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Tenofovir can put stress on the kidneys and lower bone density over time, which is why routine check-ups are so important. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h5)

question: Which breathing condition is most commonly treated with a steam tent?

options.A: Pulmonary embolism
options.B: Croup
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: You got it! Croup causes that classic barking cough, and warm, moist air is one of the best ways to bring relief. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which specific bacterium causes cholera?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Salmonella typhi
options.C: Vibrio cholerae
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Great recall! Cholera is caused by *Vibrio cholerae*, a bacterium that loves to hitch a ride in contaminated water and food supplies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T21#GNS214_U1_T21_h3)

question: Which protein in the blood has the shortest half-life, making it the best choice for checking recent, short-term changes in a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Prealbumin
options.D: Transferrin

explanation: Prealbumin breaks down and builds back up really fast. This makes it a fantastic tool to show if your patient's recent meals are working within just a couple of days! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h2)

question: Which part of the digestive tract does ulcerative colitis mainly affect?

options.A: The entire small intestine
options.B: The colon and rectum
options.C: The mouth and esophagus
options.D: The stomach and duodenum

explanation: Ulcerative colitis stays in the large intestine. It starts down in the rectum and can spread upward in a steady, continuous line. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h3)

question: What happens to the pelvic floor as the uterus grows heavier in the third trimester?

options.A: It pulls the pelvic floor upward to relieve stress on the bladder
options.B: It has no mechanical impact until actual labor begins
options.C: It places constant downward pressure that stretches the muscle fibers
options.D: It strengthens the muscles by forcing them to contract continuously

explanation: Well done! Gravity and a growing baby mean continuous downward pressure, which can stretch and tire out these hardworking muscles over time. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h2)

question: A client in a Nigerian teaching hospital demands to see their medical case notes after a surgery. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Facilitate access to the medical records following the hospital's proper administrative process
options.B: Refuse firmly because hospital files belong exclusively to the doctors and nurses
options.C: Burn the records immediately to protect the privacy of the surgical team
options.D: Tell the client that reading medical notes is illegal for ordinary citizens

explanation: Clients have the legal right to view their own medical records through the established institutional procedures. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h3)

question: Which symptom should the nurse instruct the patient to report immediately after arthrocentesis?

options.A: Feeling thirsty after the test
options.B: Fever and worsening joint pain
options.C: Mild itching around the bandage
options.D: Slight drowsiness from resting

explanation: Fever and increasing pain are key warning signs of a developing joint infection after the procedure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h7)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a newborn's blood sugar is too low (hypoglycemia)?

options.A: Jitteriness and poor muscle tone
options.B: Rapid weight gain within hours
options.C: A deep, steady, and loud cry
options.D: Sudden flushing and pink skin

explanation: When blood sugar drops, a baby's nervous system acts up, often showing as jitteriness, shaking, or feeling unusually limp. Always report this right away! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h8)

question: As a nurse leader in a public hospital, what does public accountability mainly mean for you?

options.A: Ensuring doctors follow instructions given by senior nurse managers
options.B: Answering for actions, resource use, and care quality in public facilities
options.C: Raising private funds to run hospital wards without government help
options.D: Fulfilling personal career goals within a healthcare organization

explanation: Spot on! Public accountability simply means you take responsibility for how public funds, hospital supplies, and patient care are handled on your watch. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h1)

question: What is a key characteristic of bone pain caused by osteomyelitis?

options.A: It completely disappears when the patient rests in bed
options.B: It shifts to a different bone every few hours
options.C: It is a constant, throbbing pain that worsens with movement
options.D: It only occurs when the patient eats cold foods

explanation: Bone pain from infection is typically deep, constant, throbbing, and intensified by physical activity or pressure on the site. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: You check the drug label against the doctor's prescription order. Which 'right' are you making sure of?

options.A: Right Dose
options.B: Right Time
options.C: Right Route
options.D: Right Medication

explanation: Comparing the label directly to the prescription order is your foolproof way to confirm you've grabbed the exact right drug. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is a primary responsibility of a nurse-midwife during antenatal care visits?

options.A: Manufacturing iron and vitamin supplements
options.B: Performing major obstetric surgeries at primary clinics
options.C: Educating mothers on danger signs and proper nutrition
options.D: Building new roads for easy transport to hospitals

explanation: Nurse-midwives play a key role in health education, teaching women what to expect and when to seek urgent help. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h6)

question: A patient on IV quinine for severe malaria reports dizziness and ringing in the ears. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Assume this is a normal side effect and document it routinely
options.B: Notify the prescriber and evaluate for signs of quinine toxicity
options.C: Stop the intravenous line permanently without telling anyone
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink large volumes of cold water

explanation: Spot on! These are classic signs of cinchonism (quinine toxicity). The doctor must be informed right away to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main job of 'inclusion criteria' in a nursing research study?

options.A: To explain how data will be analyzed using statistical software
options.B: To define the specific traits a participant must have to join the study
options.C: To list the reasons why a patient should be given extra medication
options.D: To describe the equipment used to measure patient vital signs

explanation: You nailed it! Inclusion criteria are simply the 'welcome checklist' of traits a person must have to be part of your research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h3)

question: When measuring fluid from a drainage container, how should the nurse read the volume accurately?

options.A: By guessing the amount based on how full the bulb looks
options.B: By weighing the container on a bathroom scale while wet
options.C: By holding the container high up near the ceiling lights
options.D: At eye level with the liquid resting on a flat surface

explanation: Reading fluid levels at eye level on a flat surface prevents parallax errors and ensures the measurement recorded on the chart is correct. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: A patient with coronary artery disease develops a sudden irregular heartbeat. What is the link between the disease and this rhythm change?

options.A: Coronary blockages directly destroy the sinoatrial node cells
options.B: Ischemia damages the heart's electrical conduction pathways
options.C: Narrowed arteries cause the heart to beat faster to compensate
options.D: Fatty plaques physically block electrical signals from traveling

explanation: When coronary arteries are narrowed, the heart muscle gets less oxygen (ischemia). Stressed, oxygen-starved heart cells have a hard time passing electrical signals smoothly, leading to irregular rhythms. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h2)

question: Your patient just woke up from surgery and feels dizzy. What should you do about getting them out of bed?

options.A: Use a standard sliding board without help
options.B: Ask the patient to walk alone to test their strength
options.C: Lift the patient quickly to avoid bedsores
options.D: Postpone the transfer and reassess the dizziness

explanation: Dizziness is a warning sign of weakness or low blood pressure. It's always safer to let them rest until they are steady. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T6#GNS112_U4_T6_h2)

question: How does an occupational therapist mostly differ from a physiotherapist?

options.A: Occupational therapists focus on adapting practical daily life tasks and home environments
options.B: Occupational therapists only work in intensive care units
options.C: Occupational therapists are licensed to prescribe medications
options.D: Occupational therapists deal exclusively with mental health disorders

explanation: While physiotherapists focus on body movement and strength, occupational therapists help patients master everyday chores like cooking, washing, and dressing. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which layer of the epidermis is busy making new skin cells and producing melanin for color?

options.A: Stratum basale
options.B: Stratum corneum
options.C: Stratum granulosum
options.D: Stratum spinosum

explanation: You got it! The stratum basale is the deepest layer of the epidermis where cell division happens constantly, and special cells called melanocytes make our skin pigment. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient experiences a sudden drop in systemic blood pressure. Which vessel directly supplies blood into the glomerulus for filtration?

options.A: Efferent arteriole
options.B: Afferent arteriole
options.C: Peritubular capillary
options.D: Interlobular vein

explanation: The afferent arteriole brings blood directly into the glomerular capillary bed to generate the pressure needed for filtration. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is your main priority as a nurse right after skeletal traction is removed?

options.A: Supporting the limb carefully to prevent sudden pain or injury
options.B: Removing the patient's compression stockings and bed rest orders
options.C: Discharging the patient home immediately
options.D: Scrubbing the old pin sites with strong iodine to remove all scars

explanation: Brilliant! Once the traction is gone, the limb is unsupported and vulnerable. Always handle the limb with extra care to keep the patient safe and comfortable. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the main goal of turning cystine into cysteine-drug complexes?

options.A: The drug permanently neutralizes all urinary calcium
options.B: The complexes completely stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: The body can reabsorb the new complexes safely in the loop of Henle
options.D: The new complexes dissolve much more easily in urine

explanation: By changing the chemical structure, the drug makes cystine soluble so it can comfortably wash out in the urine instead of forming painful stones. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T4#GNS223_U8_T4_h2)

question: Why is it important to check blood clotting lab results before a dilation procedure?

options.A: To assess the risk of bleeding from potential mucosal tears
options.B: To check if the patient has an active systemic infection
options.C: To calculate the exact dosage of local anesthetic required
options.D: To determine the correct size of the dilator to be used

explanation: Stretching tight tissues can sometimes cause minor scratches or tears. If a patient has poor blood clotting, those little tears could turn into heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h4)

question: Which symptom should immediately alert a nurse to a possible ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Painful burning when passing urine
options.B: Itching and thick white vaginal discharge
options.C: One-sided lower belly pain and abnormal spotting
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Pelvic pain on just one side, combined with light bleeding during early pregnancy, is a classic warning sign we always watch out for. Excellent! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h5)

question: What is the medical reason for performing Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhancement of fertility during childbearing years
options.B: Reduction of congenital reproductive abnormalities
options.C: Prevention of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: There is no medical justification for the procedure

explanation: You got this! FGM has zero health benefits. It's done purely for cultural or social reasons based on myths, not science. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is a core day-to-day duty of nurses and midwives in Nigerian reproductive health care?

options.A: Providing direct clinical care, health education, and community outreach
options.B: Writing national health insurance laws in the federal legislature
options.C: Manufacturing contraceptive implants in national laboratories
options.D: Importing specialized surgical instruments from overseas

explanation: Exactly! Nurses and midwives are on the frontline, delivering care at the bedside and educating communities on healthy living. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h6)

question: What special addition is often necessary when a patient is placed on a very strict low protein diet?

options.A: High-sodium tablets to maintain blood pressure
options.B: Essential amino acid or keto acid supplements
options.C: Concentrated liquid sugar for quick energy
options.D: Extra doses of water-soluble vitamins only

explanation: Strict restriction removes too many vital building blocks, so medical supplements are added to prevent the body from breaking down its own muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h3)

question: What is the term for the grief family members feel *before* a terminally ill loved one actually passes away?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Perceived grief
options.C: Complicated grief
options.D: Masked grief

explanation: Anticipatory grief happens ahead of an expected loss, which actually gives loved ones a bit of time to process their emotions early. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why do community health nurses spend time educating the public?

options.A: To replace formal school teachers in local primary classrooms
options.B: To empower individuals and groups with knowledge to prevent illness
options.C: To test public speaking skills during routine ward rounds
options.D: To fulfill mandatory administrative writing quotas

explanation: Spot on! Education is one of our most powerful tools. When people understand how diseases spread and how to live healthily, they can take charge of their own wellbeing. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is the main physiological purpose of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing bile salts to help break down dietary fats
options.B: Absorbing remaining water and compacting indigestible waste
options.C: Digesting complex proteins into single amino acids
options.D: Secreting hydrochloric acid to kill swallowed bacteria

explanation: By the time food residue gets to the colon, most nutrients are already gone. The large intestine's main task is to suck back the water and turn waste into solid stool. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h7)

question: What is the very first action a nurse must take when managing an active adverse drug reaction?

options.A: Discharging the patient home for proper rest
options.B: Calling the pharmaceutical manufacturing company
options.C: Starting broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately
options.D: Stopping the administration of the suspected drug

explanation: You've got this! Removing the source of the trouble is always the immediate step to protect your patient from further harm. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h5)

question: Which Nigerian agency is well known for regulating food and drug safety?

options.A: JAMB
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: NYSC
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is our main regulatory body for food and drugs in Nigeria. Proudly Nigerian nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h6)

question: What exactly is caregiver burnout?

options.A: A state of physical, emotional, and mental exhaustion from long-term caregiving
options.B: A sudden financial profit gained from running a home care agency
options.C: A formal medical diagnosis of dementia given to family members
options.D: A temporary feeling of tiredness after cleaning the house

explanation: Caregiving is heavy work. Burnout happens when looking after a loved one drains all physical and emotional energy without enough rest. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h7)

question: What happens in the body during an episode of obstructive sleep apnea?

options.A: Repetitive collapse of the upper pharyngeal airway during sleep
options.B: Severe inflammation of the inner ear vestibular system
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the diaphragm muscle in the chest
options.D: Sudden accumulation of cerumen blocking the nasal passages

explanation: When the throat muscles relax too much during sleep, the airway temporarily collapses and closes. This causes loud snoring and sudden pauses in breathing. Rest easy knowing you understand this concept now! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why is it so vital to write down moulding details accurately on the partograph?

options.A: It proves that the nurse gave pain medication at the correct time
options.B: It replaces the need to check the fetal heart rate during the second stage
options.C: It serves as a legal receipt for the hospital fees charged to the patient
options.D: It gives the healthcare team a clear visual trend of whether labour is becoming obstructed

explanation: The partograph gives everyone a quick visual story of how labour is going, helping the whole shift spot dangerous trends before they become emergencies. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h7)

question: Which of these makes a research hypothesis weak and unusable?

options.A: Matching the primary research question too closely
options.B: Being based on existing nursing theory
options.C: Predicting a negative relationship between variables
options.D: Using vague terms that cannot be measured

explanation: Keep it clear! If words are too fuzzy to measure, researchers won't be able to collect real data to check if it's true. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a social determinant of health?

options.A: The personal willpower of an individual to avoid sickness
options.B: Access to safe drinking water and sanitation
options.C: The specific genetic blood type of a patient
options.D: The brand of medication prescribed by a doctor

explanation: Social determinants are external environmental, economic, and social conditions that powerfully influence whether people stay healthy or fall ill. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the special thing about a "community of solution"?

options.A: Its members interact exclusively through mobile phone apps
options.B: It forms around a specific problem or shared health goal
options.C: It exists permanently within a single government district
options.D: It is defined strictly by natural rivers and mountains

explanation: Nice one! These groups team up specifically to tackle and solve a particular issue or health challenge together. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h3)

question: Where does fertilization of the egg by a sperm cell usually take place?

options.A: Within the lower cervical canal
options.B: Inside the main cavity of the uterus
options.C: On the outer surface of the ovary
options.D: Ampulla of the fallopian tube

explanation: The wider ampulla section of the fallopian tube provides the right space and environment for the sperm to meet and fertilize the egg. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h5)

question: In inflammatory joint conditions, what is 'pannus'?

options.A: An abnormal tissue layer that destroys cartilage and bone
options.B: Fluid accumulation in the outer layer of the skin
options.C: Thickened scar tissue formed after a surgical incision
options.D: A hard calcium crystal deposit inside the joint space

explanation: Pannus is an extra layer of bad, granulation-like tissue that grows inside the joint and slowly eats away at the cartilage and bone. You'll often see this in conditions like rheumatoid arthritis! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why does the inner lining of the small intestine contain millions of villi and microvilli?

options.A: To secrete large amounts of digestive enzymes straight into the mouth
options.B: To maximize the surface area available for absorbing nutrients
options.C: To produce strong muscular contractions for moving food forward
options.D: To neutralize the acidic chyme coming directly from the stomach

explanation: The villi and microvilli create a massive surface area that allows digested food particles to pass efficiently into the blood and lymph vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the main feature of a Type A adverse drug reaction?

options.A: It is predictable and depends on the size of the dose.
options.B: It never goes away even if the drug is stopped immediately.
options.C: It only happens to patients with weak immune systems.
options.D: It is completely unpredictable and has nothing to do with the dose.

explanation: Type A reactions are basically an exaggerated normal effect of the medication. Because of this, they are dose-dependent and easier to predict! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h2)

question: A community health nurse notices high rates of childhood stunting and anemia in an isolated village. What underlying distribution problem is most likely contributing to this?

options.A: An oversupply of refrigerated trucks delivering too many vegetables
options.B: Excessive availability of free nutritional supplements from clinics
options.C: Strict local laws that prohibit families from cooking traditional meals
options.D: Inability to consistently transport diverse, fresh foods to the area

explanation: Poor transport links starve remote populations of the varied nutrients required for healthy childhood development. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h7)

question: How was the role of a nurse different in early asylum days compared to modern nursing?

options.A: Nurses focused exclusively on intensive individual psychotherapy
options.B: Nurses were primarily responsible for prescribing antipsychotic medications
options.C: Nurses spent most of their time running community outreach clinics
options.D: Nurses functioned mainly as guards focused on physical containment and order

explanation: Correct! Back then, security came before healing, so nurses spent a lot of their time managing locked doors and enforcing physical control instead of therapeutic care. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h2)

question: What is the term for the process of children learning societal gender roles as they grow up?

options.A: Cellular adaptation
options.B: Socialization
options.C: Genetic mapping
options.D: Physiological maturation

explanation: Well done! Socialization is how we absorb the values, behaviors, and roles of our society through family, school, and community. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T3#GNS312_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which brain chemical is most closely linked to the reward system and feelings of pleasure?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Great job! Dopamine is the brain's main messenger for making us feel good and reinforcing rewarding behaviors. Think of it as the brain's natural 'feel-good' chemical. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h2)

question: What factor has the biggest influence on the overall survival outlook for a patient with a vulval tumour?

options.A: The stage of the cancer at the time of diagnosis
options.B: The specific brand of dressing used on the wound
options.C: The patient's personal preference for radiation therapy
options.D: The exact age of the patient during surgery

explanation: Well done! Catching the cancer early, before it spreads to the lymph nodes, gives the patient the best chance at long-term survival. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h8)

question: What nursing term is used to document painful menstrual cramps?

options.A: Amenorrhea
options.B: Dysmenorrhea
options.C: Metrorrhagia
options.D: Menorrhagia

explanation: Dysmenorrhea is just the professional word for painful periods. 'Dys' means painful or difficult, and 'menorrhea' refers to menstruation! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h7)

question: Why do freshly mixed (reconstituted) suspensions expire much faster than dry powders?

options.A: The active drug evaporates into the air inside the room
options.B: The plastic bottle begins to melt in the refrigerator
options.C: Water activates chemical breakdown and microbial growth
options.D: Refrigeration destroys the chemical bonds of the powder

explanation: Water wakes everything up! Once water is added, it triggers chemical breakdown and creates a cozy home for bacteria to multiply. That's why they don't last long. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of using reflective listening during a patient interaction?

options.A: It allows the nurse to diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders
options.B: It speeds up the assessment process so the nurse can leave
options.C: It prevents the patient from expressing negative emotions
options.D: It confirms understanding and proves to the patient that they are heard

explanation: Reflecting back what a patient says assures them that you are actively listening and accurately grasping their feelings. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which response is controlled by the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Fight-or-flight
options.B: Sleep-and-grow
options.C: Rest-and-digest
options.D: Feed-and-breed

explanation: The sympathetic system prepares the body for stressful or emergency situations, commonly known as the fight-or-flight response. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h2)

question: What does a high D-dimer blood test result usually mean?

options.A: Blood clots have recently formed and broken down in the body
options.B: The patient is not eating enough iron
options.C: There are zero platelets left in the blood
options.D: There is a sudden bacterial infection in the blood

explanation: D-dimer is a leftover protein fragment when a clot dissolves. If it's high, it tells us clotting and breakdown have been happening recently. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is knowing the exact date of a patient's last menstrual period (LMP) so important?

options.A: It proves the patient has reached full menopause
options.B: It establishes a baseline for dating a pregnancy or spotting cycle changes
options.C: It indicates the exact day ovulation will occur next month
options.D: It measures the total amount of iron stored in the blood

explanation: You will use this all the time in clinic! The LMP helps us calculate expected due dates for pregnant mums and spot any unusual bleeding patterns early. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h3)

question: As a nursing student, why is it helpful to know different research categories?

options.A: To write prescriptions for patients independently
options.B: To diagnose complex diseases without a doctor
options.C: To replace hands-on clinical ward practice
options.D: To decide if a study can guide safe patient care

explanation: Spot on! Knowing research categories helps you evaluate evidence so you can confidently apply safe, proven ideas when caring for your patients. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is a very common emotional challenge for people dealing with untreated hearing loss?

options.A: Improved cognitive processing
options.B: Heightened sense of euphoria
options.C: Increased physical strength
options.D: Social isolation and depression

explanation: When it's hard to hear conversations, people often start pulling away from social gatherings, which can lead to loneliness and depression. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T14#GNS324_U4_T14_h7)

question: What usually happens on the ward when a nurse struggles with poor time management?

options.A: Decreased physical fatigue among nursing staff
options.B: Higher patient satisfaction scores across the unit
options.C: Increased risk of missed care and medication errors
options.D: More time available for professional development

explanation: True! When things get too rushed and we lose control of our time, important tasks or meds can easily slip through the cracks. Take a breath—learning how to pace yourself helps prevent this! [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is integrating family planning into primary healthcare centers important?

options.A: It removes the need for community health education programs.
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to work in large hospitals.
options.C: It ensures that even rural and remote communities can access services.
options.D: It makes contraceptive services exclusively available to the wealthy.

explanation: Primary health centers are right in the communities. Bringing family planning there means even folks in remote villages can easily get the care and advice they need. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h4)

question: The Thomas-Kilmann conflict model is built on which two main personal behaviors?

options.A: Speed and accuracy
options.B: Assertiveness and cooperativeness
options.C: Empathy and detachment
options.D: Aggression and passivity

explanation: This model simply looks at two things: how much you push for your own needs versus how much you try to help the other person. [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h3)

question: How often should you check a stable newborn's vital signs right after birth?

options.A: Every 30 minutes until stable for two hours
options.B: Every 15 minutes for the first 24 hours
options.C: Only when the baby begins to cry or feed
options.D: Once every hour throughout the entire hospital stay

explanation: Keep a close eye on them! Vitals should be checked every half hour until the baby maintains steady vitals for a solid two hours. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h8)

question: Why do we perform a thorough baseline assessment when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any further nursing documentation
options.B: To fulfill a mandatory billing requirement for the insurance company
options.C: To diagnose the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: To establish a clear point of comparison for future shifts

explanation: Correct! Baseline assessments give us a starting reference so we can easily spot when a patient's condition changes or when a new problem arises. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary causative organism of pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: Klebsiella pneumoniae
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.D: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation: Pulmonary tuberculosis is specifically caused by the rod-shaped bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is establishing cause and effect difficult in cross-sectional studies?

options.A: Statistical software cannot process percentages
options.B: Researchers always interview too few patients
options.C: Exposure and outcome are measured at the same time
options.D: Participants never answer questionnaires honestly

explanation: Since you check both the risk factor and the health issue at the exact same moment, it's tough to know which one happened first. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h7)

question: Who played the primary role in introducing Western-style nursing and hospitals to Nigeria during the colonial era?

options.A: Missionary societies
options.B: Military combat units
options.C: International trade unions
options.D: Local traditional rulers

explanation: Christian missions established the earliest Western hospitals and introduced formal nursing concepts to Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which two major veins join together to form the hepatic portal vein?

options.A: Superior mesenteric vein and splenic vein
options.B: Hepatic vein and inferior mesenteric vein
options.C: Internal jugular vein and subclavian vein
options.D: Inferior vena cava and renal vein

explanation: You'll find this intersection right behind the pancreas! The superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein team up to form the hepatic portal vein carrying blood right to the liver. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h2)

question: In many Nigerian homes, what hazardous substance is most commonly swallowed by young children by accident because it was stored in an empty soft drink bottle?

options.A: Kerosene
options.B: Dry fertilizer
options.C: Carbon monoxide
options.D: Surgical spirit

explanation: Spot on! Kerosene is widely used for cooking and lighting. When poured into empty soft drink bottles, kids easily mistake it for a drink and swallow it. Always remember to teach parents to use proper, labeled containers! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which set of symptoms in a postpartum mother is a strong warning sign of impending eclampsia (seizures)?

options.A: Severe headache, blurred vision, and upper tummy (epigastric) pain
options.B: Dry mouth, joint stiffness, and mild fatigue
options.C: Frequent urination, extreme thirst, and itchy skin
options.D: Cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing

explanation: Keep your eyes open for these head and tummy warning signs! They tell you severe pre-eclampsia might be progressing into dangerous seizures. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h3)

question: Why is a pulse oximeter such a helpful tool when assessing a breathless patient?

options.A: It measures the exact pressure of carbon dioxide in the blood.
options.B: It replaces the need to count the patient's respiratory rate.
options.C: It gives a quick, painless way to check oxygen levels in the blood.
options.D: It determines the primary infectious organism in the lungs.

explanation: The little finger probe lets you check oxygen levels instantly without poking the patient with a needle. Very handy in busy wards! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why must nurses treat used clinical items as places where germs actively grow?

options.A: Because hospital trash is legally classified as hazardous material automatically
options.B: Because cleaning staff refuse to handle items unless they are labeled alive
options.C: Because used items contain moisture and nutrients that help microbes multiply
options.D: Because all discarded items will immediately begin to emit toxic gases

explanation: Spot on! Things like used dressings and body fluids provide a warm, wet home full of nutrients. Germs love this and will multiply rapidly if we don't contain them properly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T7#GST114_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge faced by public health nurses in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of ultra-modern robotic surgery equipment
options.B: Navigating cultural barriers and vaccine hesitancy in communities
options.C: Funding shortages affecting routine immunization supplies
options.D: Infrastructural deficits and poor road networks in remote areas

explanation: Robotic surgery equipment is found in advanced tertiary centers, not primary health care settings, making it an incorrect challenge for public health nurses. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the controlling function in nursing management?

options.A: Recruiting new nursing staff for the facility
options.B: Monitoring performance and taking corrective action
options.C: Assigning daily bedside duties to junior nurses
options.D: Drafting the annual financial budget for the hospital

explanation: Controlling is primarily about tracking actual work against set plans and fixing mistakes when things go wrong. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: A patient falls and injures their ankle. Which region of the body is affected?

options.A: Cervical region
options.B: Lower limb
options.C: Axial region
options.D: Thoracic region

explanation: The ankle is part of the lower limb, which falls under the appendicular division of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why does community health nursing place a strong emphasis on health maintenance?

options.A: It completely eliminates all infectious diseases from a population
options.B: It shifts the nurse's job entirely to administrative desk work
options.C: It makes physical examinations completely unnecessary for adults
options.D: It reduces the need for expensive hospital care by stopping illness early

explanation: Focusing on wellness helps catch problems early and keeps people out of hospital beds. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h1)

question: What hollow tube is formed when the edges of the neural plate fold and fuse together?

options.A: Neural tube
options.B: Neural crest
options.C: Amniotic sac
options.D: Notochord

explanation: Great job! The folding and closing of the neural plate forms the hollow neural tube, which eventually becomes our central nervous system. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T1#GNS211_U3_T1_h2)

question: Besides normal vital signs, what else must a nurse check during a rehab assessment?

options.A: Functional ability and home environment safety
options.B: National health insurance policy rates
options.C: Pharmaceutical manufacturing costs
options.D: Hospital administrative budgeting records

explanation: A good rehab assessment looks at how well the patient can move around and whether their home is safe for them to return to. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h6)

question: How often should you check and record temperatures in a clinic's vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: Twice daily
options.B: Every hour
options.C: Only on weekends
options.D: Once a week

explanation: Checking temperatures twice a day helps us catch fridge issues early and keeps our vaccine supply safe for the community! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h2)

question: Which tool helps a patient who struggles to bend down to wash their lower legs and feet?

options.A: A long-handled sponge
options.B: A mechanical hoist
options.C: A standard walking frame
options.D: A raised toilet seat

explanation: Brilliant! A long-handled sponge is a simple yet clever device that lets patients reach their feet easily without straining their backs. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h5)

question: Where should a community health nurse go to first make contact with street-connected children?

options.A: Markets, motor parks, and under bridges
options.B: High-end residential neighborhood clinics
options.C: University research lecture halls
options.D: Private corporate office boardrooms

explanation: You've got it! To help street youth, outreach nurses must go directly to where these children live and hang out. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T3#GNS225_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for overcoming MBO barriers in a hospital?

options.A: Celebrating small clinical wins with the nursing team
options.B: Integrating goal tracking into existing routine staff meetings
options.C: Training managers to offer supportive guidance during reviews
options.D: Adding dozens of complex new metrics for every single shift

explanation: Adding excessive metrics increases paperwork and stress, which directly harms MBO implementation. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h7)

question: A nurse manager says, 'We must sterilize the surgical instruments every morning at 7 AM.' What kind of activity is this?

options.A: An objective
options.B: A mission
options.C: A goal
options.D: A task

explanation: Spot on! Doing a specific duty at a set time is a daily task that keeps the clinic running smoothly. [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is a well-known example of a steroid hormone?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Epinephrine

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is common in advanced bone tumors due to rapid bone breakdown?

options.A: Hypoglycemia
options.B: Hyponatremia
options.C: Hypercalcemia
options.D: Hypokalemia

question: What is a major result of a country having a high birth rate over many years?

options.A: A heavy economic dependency ratio with many young citizens
options.B: A rapid increase in the average age of the working population
options.C: An immediate shortage of geriatric care facilities
options.D: A permanent surplus of maternal hospital beds nationwide

explanation: Correct! High birth rates create a young population, meaning fewer working adults have to support many children. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for tracking down and treating the sexual partners of an infected patient?

options.A: To collect financial fines for public health registries
options.B: To prevent immediate reinfection of the original patient
options.C: To test the partners for unrelated chronic diseases
options.D: To ensure the partners report to police authorities

explanation: Partner treatment breaks the ping-pong cycle! If you treat just one person, they'll likely catch it right back from their untreated partner. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h8)

question: Why do tightly coiled hair textures often tend to feel drier than straight hair?

options.B: Frequent washing strips away the natural protective proteins
options.C: Curly hair follicles lack sebaceous glands entirely
options.D: Natural scalp oils have trouble traveling down the curved hair shaft

explanation: Because of the bends and turns in coils and curls, the natural oils from the scalp have a harder time sliding down the full length of the hair. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why are accurate nursing records about needle counts so important in a court of law?

options.A: They show how fast the surgical team can work
options.B: They prove that standard safety protocols were followed
options.C: They help the hospital calculate patient food bills
options.D: They determine the salary of the operating theatre staff

explanation: You're doing great! Clear charting is your best legal protection, proving you did your job safely and correctly. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)

question: As a nurse, what is the best approach when checking thyroid lab results for a pregnant patient?

options.A: Ignoring the thyroid panel since hormones do not affect the gland

options.C: Using pregnancy-specific reference ranges instead of standard charts
options.D: Repeating the blood draw because the results are always inaccurate

question: Why is patient confidentiality especially critical during community health data collection?

options.A: It prevents the government from spending money on printing paper
options.B: It protects personal dignity and maintains community trust in health workers
options.C: It ensures that nurses never have to speak with village leaders
options.D: It makes data analysis much faster for computer software programs

explanation: If people fear their private health details will be exposed, they will hide illnesses and avoid public clinics. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h7)

question: How does proper birth spacing directly help keep mothers safe?

options.B: By ensuring all deliveries happen exclusively at home
options.C: By guaranteeing that mothers will never experience morning sickness
options.D: By completely eliminating the need for antenatal care visits

explanation: You've got this! Proper spacing gives the uterus time to rest between pregnancies, which greatly lowers the risk of heavy bleeding (hemorrhage). Great nursing insight to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why does the nurse instruct the patient to empty their bladder right before the procedure begins?

options.A: To test the urine for hidden infection before the radiologist arrives
options.B: To make sure the patient does not need to use the restroom during the dye injection
options.C: To get an accurate baseline and prevent residual urine from blocking the view

question: Why is communication especially critical for the home health care team compared to a hospital staff?

options.A: Hospital staff do not communicate with each other during shifts
options.B: Team members work independently in scattered locations rather than in one building
options.C: Home health personnel rarely document patient progress in charts
options.D: Patients manage their own medications without professional input

explanation: Because home health workers operate separately in different homes, clear and timely communication is vital to keep everyone updated on patient status. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h1)

question: An antibiotic costs 500 Naira to land in the pharmacy, and hospital policy adds a 20 percent mark-up. What is the retail price?

options.C: 600 Naira
options.D: 700 Naira

question: What was a major issue with patients bringing bulk drug supplies to Nigerian hospital wards?

options.A: Too many digital prescription logs
options.B: Poor storage conditions and lost medications
options.C: Excessive involvement of clinical pharmacists
options.D: Immediate electronic tracking of every pill

explanation: Bulk drugs kept in ward lockers were frequently misplaced, stolen, or exposed to heat and moisture, which ruined their potency. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h2)

question: How often should you check and log the temperature of vaccine storage refrigerators?

options.A: Once a week during stock inventory
options.B: Only when a power outage occurs
options.C: Once a month during the facility meeting
options.D: Twice daily, morning and evening

explanation: Standard cold chain rules require checking and writing down fridge temperatures twice every day to catch any temperature changes early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h4)

question: How does pursed-lip breathing help someone struggling with chronic breathing problems?

options.A: It increases the heart rate to improve tissue perfusion.

options.C: It creates back-pressure that keeps small airways from collapsing when they breathe out.
options.D: It forces all carbon dioxide out of the stomach immediately.

explanation: Breathing out through pursed lips acts like a brake, keeping airways open longer so the lungs can empty out more old air. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h7)

question: Which diagnostic test is primarily used to confirm the location of a suspected ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Routine urinalysis
options.B: Abdominal X-ray scan
options.C: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: A transvaginal ultrasound allows the healthcare provider to look directly inside the uterus and fallopian tubes to see where the pregnancy has implanted. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h5)

question: What does alignment mean within the hierarchy of objectives?

options.A: Doctors and nurses must share the same university degree
options.B: All nurses must work the exact same number of day and night shifts
options.C: Every department must have the exact same financial budget
options.D: Lower-level goals directly support and connect to upper-level goals

explanation: Alignment ensures that operational, tactical, and strategic goals work together without contradiction. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which clinical sign helps you tell kwashiorkor apart from marasmus?

options.A: Bilateral pitting edema
options.B: Extreme loss of all body fat
options.C: High serum iron concentration
options.D: Rapid increase in bone length

question: Which lymphoid organ is primarily responsible for filtering blood and destroying old red blood cells?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Thymus
options.C: Liver
options.D: Tonsil

explanation: The spleen filters blood, recycles iron from hemoglobin, and removes damaged red blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of a posterior surface landmark?

options.A: Umbilicus
options.B: Inguinal crease
options.C: Sternal angle
options.D: Scapula

question: When trying to keep people safe from chemicals at work, what is considered the absolute best first step?

options.A: Conducting weekly medical tests on every worker

options.C: Putting warning signs on every single office door
options.D: Replacing a toxic chemical with a safer alternative

question: For how many months should a baby be exclusively breastfed?

options.A: The first 9 months of life
options.B: The entire first year of life
options.C: The first 6 months of life
options.D: The first 3 months of life

explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, food, and protection a baby needs for their first 6 solid months. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which intrapartum nursing action helps minimize the risk of vertical transmission during labor?

options.A: Performing frequent routine vaginal examinations
options.B: Encouraging immediate pushing during the early latent phase
options.C: Avoiding unnecessary artificial rupture of membranes
options.D: Administering oxytocin infusion to all mothers routinely

explanation: Keeping membranes intact as long as possible reduces the time the baby is exposed to infectious fluids in the birth canal. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is the main goal of an Infant Welfare Clinic?

options.A: Emergency trauma management
options.B: Surgical operations for newborns
options.C: Preventive care and health promotion
options.D: Inpatient hospital admission

explanation: You've got this! These clinics focus on stopping illnesses before they start through check-ups and immunizations, rather than treating severe hospital emergencies. Great job keeping kids healthy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T54#GNS214_U1_T54_h1)

question: A patient presents with chronic swelling in both lower legs and brownish skin discoloration around the ankles. Which underlying vascular problem is most likely responsible?

options.A: Acute plaque rupture in a major femoral artery
options.B: Chronic venous insufficiency with valve failure
options.C: Complete blockage of the deep capillary beds
options.D: Severe systemic hypotension due to dehydration

question: Which parts of the body are involved in a lower respiratory tract infection?

options.C: Oral cavity and epiglottis
options.D: Trachea, bronchi, and alveoli

question: A patient on strong pain medication reports feeling constantly queasy and unable to keep food down. What is the nurse's best initial action?

options.C: Force the patient to finish a standard hospital meal tray

question: Why must you check the expiration date on the test strip bottle before testing a patient?

options.C: Using expired strips violates hospital electricity codes
options.D: Expired strips may give incorrect readings

question: How long must symptoms last before a doctor or nurse can clinically diagnose female sexual dysfunction?

options.B: At least two weeks
options.C: Twelve months straight
options.D: One month or more

question: How are most deep placental problems, like placenta accreta, usually spotted before delivery?

options.A: Measuring maternal blood pressure twice daily
options.B: Performing a routine digital cervical examination
options.C: Routine antenatal ultrasound and color Doppler imaging

question: When does normal breast engorgement usually happen after a mother gives birth?

question: Why is case management crucial for patients receiving extensive home health services?

question: A patient keeps returning to the clinic with waterborne infections due to poor living conditions. What do these conditions represent?

question: Which of the following is a core component checked during a psychosocial evaluation?

question: How is Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) different from basic health education?

question: What is a major clinical benefit for nurses and doctors who work with an essential drug list?

question: What is the golden rule of pharmacology when giving new medications to older adults?

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics typically ordered immediately for a patient who has undergone a recent gishiri cut?
